cities.name: Kedarnath
cities.overview: A high Himalayan temple town at about 3,580 m in Rudraprayag district, reached on foot from Gaurikund and open only from spring to autumn.

cities.name: Ghangaria
cities.overview: A seasonal trekking village in Chamoli district, the overnight stop for the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib, reached by a 13 km trail from Govindghat.

cities.name: Ramnagar
cities.overview: A town in Nainital district at the gateway to Jim Corbett National Park, where most safari bookings and lodges are based.

cities.name: Haridwar
cities.overview: One of Hinduism's seven holy cities, where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya for the plains, and host of the Kumbh Mela.
cities.history: One of the seven holy cities of Hinduism, where the Ganges leaves the mountains. It hosts the Kumbh Mela every 12 years.

cities.name: Dehradun
cities.overview: Uttarakhand's capital in the Doon valley, between the Shivaliks and the Himalaya, a base for Mussoorie.
cities.history: Long a part of the Garhwal kingdom, it passed to the British after the Gurkha wars of 1814-16. They built schools, a military academy and a forestry institute here.

cities.name: Mussoorie
cities.overview: A hill station 26 km from Dehradun, with a long Mall Road and views of the Doon Valley and the snows.

cities.name: Rishikesh
cities.overview: A pilgrim town on the Ganges at the foot of the hills, known for yoga, rafting and suspension bridges.

cities.name: Nainital
cities.overview: A Kumaon lake town and the judicial capital of the state, built around a crescent-shaped lake.

cities.name: Almora
cities.overview: An old Chand dynasty capital on a Kumaon ridge, with stone-roofed streets and a view of the snows.

cities.name: Ranikhet
cities.overview: A quiet army cantonment and hill town in the Kumaon Hills, among pine and oak.

cities.name: Badrinath
cities.overview: A temple town high on the Alaknanda, and one of the four dhams of Uttarakhand.

cities.name: Joshimath
cities.overview: A town on the road to Badrinath, and the base for Auli's ski slopes.

cities.name: Uttarkashi
cities.overview: A district town on the Bhagirathi, gateway to Gangotri and Yamunotri.

cities.name: Pithoragarh
cities.overview: The far eastern district of Kumaon, on the road to Munsiyari and the Johar Valley.

cities.name: Pauri
cities.overview: A Garhwal district town, close to the cantonment of Lansdowne and the Tehri Lake road.

places.name: Kedarnath Temple
places.shortDescription: A high-altitude Jyotirlinga shrine of Shiva, one of the Char Dham, reached by a 16 km mountain trek.
places.description: The stone Kedarnath Temple stands in a glacial valley at the head of the Mandakini River, framed by snow peaks. Pilgrims walk the steep 16 km trail from Gaurikund, ride ponies or take a helicopter from Phata or Guptkashi. Registration with the Uttarakhand government is mandatory for the Char Dham yatra. The weather changes quickly at this altitude, so carry warm and waterproof clothing and acclimatise before climbing.
places.history: Kedarnath is among the twelve Jyotirlingas and the Panch Kedar temples. The present temple is traditionally associated with Adi Shankaracharya, whose samadhi lies behind it. It survived the devastating 2013 flash flood largely intact.
places.bestTimeNote: The temple opens around late April or May and closes around Bhai Dooj (October–November). Avoid the monsoon (July–August) because of landslides.

entryFee.note: Free darshan; online Char Dham registration is mandatory.

timings.hours: About 4:00 AM – 9:00 PM in the open season

places.name: Valley of Flowers National Park
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed Himalayan valley carpeted with hundreds of species of wildflowers during the monsoon.
places.description: The Valley of Flowers is a high-altitude meadow about 8 km long, reached by a day hike from Ghangaria. During the monsoon it fills with more than 500 species of flowering plants, including blue poppies, primulas, potentillas and cobra lilies, against a backdrop of waterfalls and glaciers. Overnight camping inside the park is not allowed. Many trekkers also climb to the Sikh shrine of Hemkund Sahib from Ghangaria.
places.history: British mountaineer Frank Smythe stumbled upon the valley in 1931 and made it famous through his book 'The Valley of Flowers'. It became a national park in 1982 and was added to the Nanda Devi UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005.
places.bestTimeNote: The park is open from 1 June to 31 October; mid-July to mid-August has the most flowers.

entryFee.note: Entry permit issued at the forest checkpost near Ghangaria; separate rates for Indians and foreigners.

timings.hours: Entry about 7:00 AM – noon; visitors must leave by evening

location.address: Valley of Flowers National Park, near Ghangaria, Chamoli district, Uttarakhand

places.name: Jim Corbett National Park
places.shortDescription: India's oldest national park, with tigers, elephants and the Ramganga River flowing through sal forest and grassland.
places.description: Corbett's sal forests, grasslands (chaurs) and riverbanks support tigers, leopards, Asian elephants, deer and over 500 species of birds. Jeep and canter safaris run in several zones, Bijrani and Jhirna among the most popular, while Dhikala in the heart of the park offers forest-lodge stays. Permits are booked online through the park's website and fill up early in the peak season. The Corbett Museum at Kaladhungi was the hunter-turned-conservationist's home.
places.history: Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, it was India's first national park. It was renamed in 1956 after Jim Corbett, and in 1973 became the site where Project Tiger was launched.
places.bestTimeNote: Mid-November to June. Most zones close in the monsoon; Jhirna stays open all year.

entryFee.note: Safari and Dhikala permits are booked online; prices vary by zone and nationality.

location.address: Jim Corbett National Park, Ramnagar, Nainital district, Uttarakhand 244715

places.name: Har Ki Pauri
places.shortDescription: Haridwar's most sacred ghat on the Ganga, where thousands gather for the glowing evening aarti.
places.description: Har Ki Pauri, 'the steps of the Lord', is the ghat where pilgrims bathe in the fast-flowing Ganga as it enters the plains. Every evening at sunset priests perform the Ganga aarti with great brass lamps while bells ring and devotees float leaf boats of flowers and diyas on the river. Arrive early to get a good spot on the steps or the bridge opposite. The ghat is the focal point of the Kumbh and Ardh Kumbh melas.
places.history: Tradition holds that King Vikramaditya built the ghat in memory of his brother Bhartrihari. Hindu belief marks a stone in its wall as bearing the footprint of Vishnu.
places.bestTimeNote: October to April. The Kumbh Mela (every 12 years) and Kanwar season (July) are extremely crowded.

timings.hours: Open all day; Ganga aarti at sunrise and sunset

places.name: Forest Research Institute
places.shortDescription: A grand red-brick colonial campus in Dehradun, with six forestry museums and huge lawns.
places.description: A vast Greco-Roman building set in hundreds of acres of trees, often seen in Bollywood films. The museums cover timber, insects and forest science.
places.history: An old training ground for India's forest service.

places.name: Mindrolling Monastery
places.shortDescription: A large Tibetan Buddhist monastery in Clement Town, Dehradun, with a giant golden Buddha.
places.description: The original seat is in Tibet, and the Indian monastery was rebuilt here after 1959. Its great stupa, gardens and golden Buddha are the highlight.
places.history: Mindrolling is one of the six mother monasteries of the Nyingma school, founded in Tibet in 1676.

places.name: Kempty Falls
places.shortDescription: A popular waterfall in Tehri Garhwal, 13 km from Mussoorie on the Chakrata road.
places.description: Water falls in stages into a pool that's packed with bathers in the summer season. It's crowded and commercial, but it's a Mussoorie tradition.

places.name: Landour
places.shortDescription: A small cantonment above Mussoorie, known for quiet walks, old churches and bakeries.
places.description: A loop road called the Chakkar runs through deodar forest past old bungalows and the home of writer Ruskin Bond. It's far quieter than Mussoorie itself.
places.history: Founded in the 1820s as a British military cantonment.

places.name: Dhanaulti
places.shortDescription: A pine and deodar hill station at 2,286 m, a calmer escape past Mussoorie.
places.description: An eco park, forest walks and winter snow, with the Surkanda Devi temple not far away on a high ridge.

places.name: Lakshman Jhula
places.shortDescription: A historic suspension bridge across the Ganges, the landmark of Rishikesh.
places.description: The iron footbridge has been closed to traffic since 2020 for safety reasons, but the temples, cafes and river views around it still draw crowds.

places.name: Beatles Ashram
places.shortDescription: The abandoned Chaurasi Kutia ashram, where the Beatles stayed in 1968.
places.description: Overgrown meditation domes and a huge graffiti-painted hall, now in the Rajaji reserve. It's a strange, peaceful place that's perfect for wandering.
places.history: The Beatles stayed here in 1968 to study meditation with Maharishi Mahesh Yogi.

places.name: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
places.shortDescription: A Shiva temple 32 km from Rishikesh, in the forest, at the spot where Shiva drank the poison.
places.description: A colourful temple in the hills that's visited by huge crowds of Kanwar pilgrims during the Shravan season. You can also walk there from Rishikesh on a forest path.

places.name: Rajaji National Park
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve of 820 sq km in the Sivalik Hills, between Haridwar, Dehradun and Rishikesh.
places.description: Sal forest and river beds, known for its elephants and leopards. It's the easiest wild place to reach from Delhi by rail.
places.history: Formed in 1983 by merging three wildlife sanctuaries.

places.name: Mansa Devi Temple
places.shortDescription: A hilltop goddess temple on Bilwa Parvat above Haridwar, reached on foot or by cable car.
places.description: A busy shrine on top of a Sivalik hill, where people tie threads to a sacred tree to make wishes. The cable car gives you a fine view of the Ganges.

places.name: Devprayag
places.shortDescription: The sacred meeting of the Alaknanda and Bhagirathi, where the river takes the name Ganga.
places.description: The last of the Panch Prayag, where a blue-green stream and a muddy one join in a gorge. A stone path leads down to the point where they meet.

places.name: Tehri Lake
places.shortDescription: The reservoir of India's tallest dam, on the Bhagirathi, now a water sports hub.
places.description: A vast lake that covers the old town of Tehri. Jet skis and houseboats have made it a growing adventure destination.
places.history: The 260.5 m dam drowned the old town of Tehri when the reservoir filled.

places.name: Lansdowne
places.shortDescription: A quiet cantonment town in Pauri Garhwal, home of the Garhwal Rifles.
places.description: An uncrowded hill town with old churches, pine walks and a small regimental museum. It's a favourite quiet weekend from Delhi.
places.history: Named after Lord Lansdowne, Viceroy of India.

places.name: Naini Lake
places.shortDescription: The crescent-shaped lake at the heart of Nainital, surrounded by steep wooded hills.
places.description: Boats drift past the Naina Devi Temple, and the Mall Road follows the whole of one shore. The cable car gives you a view of the snows.
places.history: A natural freshwater lake that's tectonic in origin.

places.name: Bhimtal
places.shortDescription: A larger, quieter lake town 22 km from Nainital, with an island aquarium.
places.description: A calmer alternative to Nainital, with paragliding at Bhowali and a small island in the lake that has an aquarium.

places.name: Mukteshwar
places.shortDescription: A Kumaon hill village at 2,171 m, with orchards and the Himalaya from Chauli ki Jali.
places.description: Fruit orchards and an old Shiva temple sit on a ridge facing the high peaks. It's a quiet stop, with some rock climbing and a British veterinary institute.

places.name: Ranikhet
places.shortDescription: A pine-shaded Kumaon cantonment with one of India's highest golf courses, at Upat.
places.description: Quiet walks among deodar and pine, with the Kumaon Regiment's museum and a Himalayan view that's among the best anywhere.

places.name: Kausani
places.shortDescription: A small hill station with a 300 km panorama of peaks like Nanda Devi and Panchachuli.
places.description: Tea gardens and pine woods look out over one of the widest Himalayan views anywhere. Mahatma Gandhi stayed here and called it the Switzerland of India.

images.credit: Abhijit Kar Gupta from Kolkata, India

places.name: Jageshwar
places.shortDescription: A group of over 100 old stone temples in a deodar forest near Almora.
places.description: Ancient temples with stone towers stand under huge deodars in a quiet valley, and they're managed by the Archaeological Survey of India. It's one of the Dhams of Shaivism.
places.history: Most of the temples date from the 9th to the 13th century.

places.name: Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A forest sanctuary on a ridge north of Almora, with oak woods, birds and a Himalayan view.
places.description: A quiet reserve with trails through oak and rhododendron, and over 200 bird species. Zero Point gives you a 300 km view of the snows.
places.history: Binsar was the summer capital of the Chand kings of Kumaon.

places.name: Munsiyari
places.shortDescription: A high Kumaon village in Pithoragarh, facing the Panchachuli peaks, and a base for glacier treks.
places.description: A Himalayan outpost at the head of the Johar Valley, with some of the best close-up views of the Panchachuli range. Milam and Ralam glacier treks start here.

places.name: Badrinath Temple
places.shortDescription: The temple of Vishnu in Chamoli, one of the Char Dham, on the Alaknanda at about 3,100 m.
places.description: A brightly painted facade against bare peaks, with hot springs below it. It's a major pilgrimage in the Himalaya, open for around six months of the year.
places.history: One of the 108 Divya Desams, sacred to Vaishnavas.
places.bestTimeNote: Open roughly from April or May to November, depending on the snow.

places.name: Gangotri
places.shortDescription: A temple town at the head of the Bhagirathi, and the source of the Ganges in Hindu tradition.
places.description: A white temple beside the roaring Bhagirathi. Serious pilgrims trek on to Gaumukh, the glacier snout at the true source.
places.bestTimeNote: Open roughly from April or May to November, depending on the snow.

places.name: Yamunotri Temple
places.shortDescription: A temple to the Yamuna at 3,291 m, reached by a 5 km walk, one of the Char Dham.
places.description: A small temple with a black marble idol of Yamuna, reached by a steep path. Pilgrims cook rice in the hot springs.
places.bestTimeNote: Open roughly from April or May to November, depending on the snow.

places.name: Tungnath
places.shortDescription: One of the world's highest Shiva temples and the highest of the Panch Kedar, in Rudraprayag.
places.description: A short steep trek from Chopta goes through meadows to an old stone temple, and on to Chandrashila summit. It's one of the best short treks in the Himalaya.

places.name: Auli
places.shortDescription: India's premier ski slope in Chamoli, at about 2,800 m, with views of Nanda Devi.
places.description: Long ski runs on a meadow with a view of Nanda Devi, and one of Asia's longest cable cars from Joshimath. Summer brings green meadows.

places.name: Gurdwara Hemkund Sahib
places.shortDescription: A high Sikh shrine beside a glacial lake, reached on foot from Ghangaria.
places.description: A steep trek ends at a star-shaped gurdwara beside a lake at over 4,000 m, in a ring of snow. It's among the highest gurdwaras in the world.
places.history: Devoted to Guru Gobind Singh, and it's mentioned in the Dasam Granth.
places.bestTimeNote: Open only from about June to October.

places.name: Roopkund
places.shortDescription: The Skeleton Lake at 5,020 m in Chamoli, with old human bones visible when the ice melts.
places.description: A hard high-altitude trek that crosses Ali and Bedni Bugyal meadows on the way. The remains by the lake have puzzled scientists for decades.
places.bestTimeNote: Forest department rules on access to the lake have changed in recent years, so check before you go.

places.name: Har Ki Dun
places.shortDescription: A cradle-shaped hanging valley in the Garhwal Himalaya, reached on a classic moderate trek.
places.description: A long walk through old wooden villages and forests, ending in a meadow ringed with peaks. It's a popular first high-altitude trek.

places.name: Nanda Devi National Park
places.shortDescription: A UNESCO park around India's second-highest peak, in Chamoli, closed to most visitors.
places.description: A huge natural basin of peaks and glaciers, closed to most visitors to protect its rare habitat, though Lata Kharak offers fine views. It shares its UNESCO listing with the Valley of Flowers.
